messages:
Mateo (ENG): Hey team, need help coordinating parental leave. We're expecting in November and Im planning 12 weeks off. Im also asking about the international leave top-up for UK-based partners (we're dual-citizenship). How do I apply and what paperwork is needed?

Priya (People Ops): Congrats!! :tada: For international top-ups: submit the Parental Leave Top-Up form and attach proof of residency/employment for the partner if outside the US. Link: https://hr.internal.redwood/top-up. We need the due date, expected leave dates, and copies of any local statutory leave award if applicable.

Mateo (ENG): Thanks. Do we need to provide translations if documents are in Spanish?

Priya (People Ops): Short answer: yes, please provide certified translations for non-English legal docs. We can accept a translated PDF and the original. People Ops can reimburse translation costs under the family benefits policy (use code "TRANS-LEAVE" when submitting receipts).

Mateo (ENG): Great. Also: tax withholding? Will the top-up be processed through payroll or as reimbursement?

Sam (Finance): Hi Mateo : top-ups are payroll-coded supplemental pay, so they go through payroll and may be taxable depending on your country. For UK residents, some elements may be taxable; we'll compute withholding when we process payroll. If you want an estimate, DM me the rough schedule and amounts and Ill run a calc.

Evelyn (Manager): From a team planning perspective: Mateo, can you draft a 6-week handoff plan for the immediate post-birth period? Recruiting can help identify a short-term contractor for 8-10 weeks if we need extra coverage.

Mateo (ENG): Will do. One more: what's the policy on company laptop returns during leave? I might go abroad for a few weeks and need to take it with me.

Priya (People Ops): Company equipment can be taken abroad with manager sign-off and an equipment travel form. If youre taking devices outside the US, fill the Equipment Travel form and note duration/countries. Also check export control if traveling to restricted countries (we'll flag any issues).

Mateo (ENG): Not restricted, just Spain for family time.

Priya (People Ops): Perfect, just complete the form and attach your phased-return plan if you're doing partial weeks.

RecruitingBot: Recruiting note: temporary contractor requests need role summary + must-have skills + duration + hourly budget. Typical posting time after approval is 48-72h. Tag @recruiting when ready.

Mateo (ENG): Quick follow-ups: 1) Can top-up start after statutory leave ends (so it's sequential)? 2) If partner takes unpaid leave in their country, does that affect our top-up?

Priya (People Ops): 1) Yes, top-up can be scheduled to start after statutory leave; specify dates on the form. 2) We need documentation of the partner's leave status. If partner takes unpaid leave, that does not automatically disqualify the employee, but we may ask for proof to coordinate benefit timing.

Sam (Finance): Also flag: for dual-citizenship cases we'll check cross-border tax treaties; might ask you to complete a short tax residency questionnaire.

Mateo (ENG): Awesome, thanks. I'll fill the top-up form and upload docs. Evelyn, I'll send the handoff and dates by EOD.

Evelyn (Manager): Thanks Mateo. Happy to review the handoff and approve equipment travel.

Priya (People Ops): Filing note: Please include HR case number on the form once created. If anyone needs help with translations or payroll estimates, ping me or Sam directly.
